items.d: One place to raise an HR request, with routing, SLAs and a visible trail.

detail.thesis:
Problem Space

Employee HR support is often handled through a combination of emails, calls, messages and basic request tracking. This can result in unclear ownership, inconsistent routing and prioritization, repeated employee follow-ups, limited visibility of request progress, and difficulty measuring HR service performance.

As organizations grow, HR teams need a structured and measurable way to manage employee support requests with clear ownership, service expectations, communication and accountability.

Solution Scope

Evolve the existing PHR Request Tracker into a comprehensive Employee Help Desk / HR Service Management capability.

The solution will provide employees with a single place to raise, communicate about and track HR service requests, while enabling HR teams to route, prioritize, assign, manage and measure requests throughout their lifecycle. The existing Request Tracker should be reused and enhanced wherever possible rather than creating a separate overlapping solution.

List of Items
  • HR Service Catalogue — Categories, Subcategories and Request Types
  • Configurable Request Forms / Templates
  • Handling Groups and Request Routing
  • Assignment and Reassignment
  • Impact, Urgency and Priority Management
  • SLA Profiles, Warnings and Breach Management
  • Configurable Approval Workflows
  • Employee–HR Conversation with Public Replies and Internal Notes
  • Attachments and Request-for-Information flow
  • Employee My Requests and request-status timeline
  • HR Handler Queue / Workbench
  • Request lifecycle management — New to Resolution, Closure and Reopening
  • Lifecycle Notifications
  • Employee Feedback
  • HR Service Dashboards and Analytics

items.d: Approve and act on workflow tasks from WhatsApp, without entering PHR.

detail.thesis:
Problem Space

Many HR workflows depend on timely actions from managers, supervisors and approvers who may not regularly use PHR. When they need to enter the HR system separately to find and complete individual workflow tasks, approvals can be delayed, requests remain pending, bottlenecks build up, and HR teams spend additional effort sending reminders and following up.

The business need is to reduce avoidable workflow delays by bringing the required task and permitted action closer to the responsible user at the time action is needed.

Solution Scope

Enable authorized users to receive PHR workflow tasks through supported messaging platforms and perform permitted workflow actions directly from that interaction.

The messaging platform acts only as an interaction channel. PHR remains the workflow engine and source of truth, controlling the valid actions, permissions, validations, workflow state and audit history. The initial direction identifies WhatsApp as the first supported platform, with the architecture designed to support additional messaging platforms later.

List of Items
  • Workflow task notifications through supported messaging platforms
  • Initial WhatsApp support with extensible multi-platform architecture
  • Workflow task and recipient identification
  • Secure messaging-user-to-PHR-user identification
  • Existing PHR authorization and organizational-scope enforcement
  • Display of relevant workflow task context
  • Dynamic retrieval of currently valid workflow actions
  • Approve
  • Reject
  • Send Back
  • Request More Information
  • Collection of mandatory comments, reasons or additional information
  • Execution through the existing PHR workflow engine
  • Preservation of existing validations, workflow sequencing and state
  • Validation of expired or changed workflow tasks
  • Workflow action confirmation
  • Workflow audit trail within PHR
  • Notification and action delivery/status tracking

items.d: Ask workforce questions from Teams, WhatsApp or Google Chat.

detail.thesis:
Problem Space

C-level and senior management users such as CEOs, CFOs and CHROs frequently need workforce information during business discussions and decision-making, but they may not regularly access PHR or navigate into an HR analytics application.

As a result, workforce intelligence can remain disconnected from the discussions where it is most valuable. Executives may need to switch systems or depend on HR teams to retrieve information for them, slowing decision-making and reducing the practical adoption of workforce analytics.

Solution Scope

Extend the existing PHR AI Insights capability to supported messaging and collaboration platforms so authorized executives can ask workforce-related questions in natural language and receive relevant insights directly within the communication environment they already use.

The messaging platform will act only as an additional interaction channel. AI Insights remains the intelligence and security layer, applying the same data permissions, organizational scope and analytical logic available within PHR.

List of Items
  • AI Insights access through supported messaging platforms
  • Executive workforce questions using natural language
  • Conversational follow-up questions
  • Workforce summaries and management-level analysis
  • Headcount, absenteeism, turnover and other available workforce insights
  • Predictive insights where supported by AI Insights
  • AI-generated recommendations where available
  • Tables, charts or simplified visualizations where supported by the channel
  • Secure messaging-user-to-PHR-user identification
  • Existing AI Insights permissions and organizational-scope enforcement
  • Client-specific data availability enforcement
  • Conversation context and continuity
  • Sensitive workforce information protection
  • Summary responses for complex analytical results
  • Link back to full AI Insights for deeper analysis
  • Reusable architecture for multiple messaging platforms

items.d: One conversational interface across the whole platform, not another module.

detail.thesis:
Problem Space

PHR continues to grow with more modules, workflows and capabilities, but users still need to understand where functionality exists, which screens to use and how individual processes work. This creates increasing complexity and limits how easily users can consume the full value of the platform.

Traditional UI-driven interaction also restricts users to the way individual screens and processes have been designed. Activities that involve large volumes of data, multiple steps or repeated transactions can require significant manual effort.

The opportunity is to move beyond screen-based HRIS interaction and enable users to simply tell PHR what they want to achieve, allowing the platform to understand the intent, collect the necessary inputs and securely perform the work on their behalf.

Solution Scope

Establish a single Agentic Platform/interface across PHR where users can naturally communicate with and operate the system.

The target is for the platform to ultimately support any activity an authorized user can perform through the PHR UI, while also enabling new ways of working that are difficult or inefficient through traditional screens.

For example, instead of creating employees individually, a user could upload an Excel file and instruct PHR to create all employees. The platform would interpret the data, apply the relevant PHR configurations and validations, identify issues, obtain confirmation where required and execute the transactions.

The interaction should support more than text, including Excel/CSV files, documents, attachments, images and voice inputs wherever they form part of a PHR activity.

A primary capability of the platform should be user-created Agents, allowing users to create reusable AI workers for their own recurring or specialized activities using the PHR capabilities available to them.

PHR remains the underlying system of record, with existing permissions, organizational access, client configurations, business validations and workflows continuing to govern what can be executed.

List of Items
  • Single Agentic Interface across PHR
  • Natural-language interaction and execution
  • Execution of existing PHR UI capabilities
  • Cross-module and multi-step task execution
  • Bulk operations beyond current UI limitations
  • Excel / CSV-driven transactions and bulk processing
  • File and document-based inputs
  • Attachment submission within applicable transactions
  • Voice-based instructions and submissions
  • Intelligent collection of missing information
  • Existing PHR validation and workflow execution
  • Preview and confirmation for applicable actions
  • Validation-error identification, correction and retry
  • User-created Agents
  • Agent configuration for specific responsibilities and recurring work
  • Reusable Agent execution
  • Role- and permission-aware Agent behaviour
  • Execution history and auditability
  • Extensible foundation for progressively onboarding PHR capabilities

items.d: Heavy reports process in the background while light ones stay instant.

detail.thesis:
Problem Space

As client data volumes, reporting periods and report complexity increase, some reports require significantly more processing time than others. When these reports are generated through the same immediate-processing model, users may spend unnecessary time waiting, remain uncertain about report status, submit duplicate requests, and experience reduced confidence in the reporting process.

Resource-intensive reporting can also place additional pressure on application resources and become increasingly difficult to scale as PHR supports larger clients and greater historical data volumes.

Solution Scope

Introduce a hybrid report-generation model within the existing Report Navigator.

PHR should automatically determine the processing load of each report and select the appropriate execution method:

  • Lower-load reports continue to generate immediately.
  • Higher-load reports are generated asynchronously in the background, allowing the user to continue working in PHR.

Once a background report is completed, the requesting user should be notified through PHR and, where applicable, by email with a secure link to View or Download the report.

Report Navigator should remain the primary location for viewing report-processing status and accessing generated reports.

The solution should also define a secure approach for storing, accessing, retaining and removing asynchronously generated report files, including client isolation, report permissions, requesting-user access and secure delivery of generated outputs. The existing proposal already identifies retention, storage implications and security as discovery areas.

List of Items
  • Report processing-load classification / load index
  • Automatic synchronous vs asynchronous execution decision
  • Immediate generation for lower-load reports
  • Background processing for higher-load reports
  • Background report-processing queue
  • Generating / Ready / Failed report statuses
  • Ability to continue using PHR while reports are generated
  • Report completion notification within PHR
  • Email notification for completed background reports
  • Secure View / Download Report link
  • View and download completed reports through Report Navigator
  • Failure reason where available
  • Retry capability for failed report generation
  • Duplicate report-request prevention / warning
  • Report-generation history
  • Secure storage of generated reports
  • Client / tenant isolation of generated files
  • Requesting-user and existing report-permission enforcement
  • Secure link access and expiry rules
  • Report retention and automatic file cleanup
  • Storage management for generated outputs
  • Access / download auditability
  • Handling of permission changes after report generation
  • Report Navigator as the source of truth for report status and completed outputs

items.d: Employee self service through the chat apps people already use.

detail.thesis:
Problem Space

Employees frequently need simple HR information or self-service support such as checking leave balances, understanding policies, reviewing attendance information or completing common HR transactions. However, they may still need to open PHR, find the correct module or screen and understand the relevant process.

For occasional HRIS users, this creates unnecessary effort and can lead to continued dependency on HR teams for information and services that are already available through digital self-service.

Solution Scope

Extend the existing Lexi conversational experience to supported messaging platforms, allowing employees to access HR knowledge, retrieve authorized employee information and perform supported self-service transactions through natural conversation.

The messaging platform should act only as another interaction channel. Lexi and PHR remain responsible for understanding the request, collecting required information, applying validations and permissions, executing the transaction and returning the result.

For transactional activities, Lexi should collect all required information, validate the request and present a clear confirmation before making any change in PHR.

Concise List of Items
  • Lexi access through supported messaging platforms
  • Natural-language HR queries and self-service interaction
  • HR policy and document questions
  • Organizational and contextual HR guidance
  • Leave balance and other authorized employee information
  • Attendance information
  • Supported employee self-service transactions
  • Collection of required transaction information
  • Existing PHR validations and business-rule enforcement
  • Transaction preview and confirmation before execution
  • Success / failure response after transaction processing
  • Secure messaging-account-to-PHR-employee identification
  • Existing employee permissions and eligibility enforcement
  • Client-specific configuration and capability controls
  • Sensitive employee-information protection
  • Conversation and session management
  • Session expiry and re-authentication where required
  • Client-level enable / disable controls
  • Control over which Lexi capabilities are exposed externally
  • Transaction and audit history within PHR
  • Extensible architecture for additional supported messaging platforms

general:
External systems
  • Integrations are built per customer, not offered by the platform. Each one is paid for once rather than holding the account, and a competitor rebuilds the set in a single implementation.

Statutory depth in Payroll and Attendance
  • Statutory rules live in per-customer configuration, not in the platform. Every change is rebuilt account by account, so no customer is safer for being on PeoplesHR.

Platform usage monitoring
